name_reason: Name follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention and accurately reflects the body: it pans the battle camera/cursor to a runtime character's tile. No Ghidra address residue; no trailing hex. The 'char' refers to a runtime character (indexed by char_idx), which is correct domain semantics, not a literal C char type.
purpose: Convenience wrapper that pans the animated battle cursor/camera to the tile occupied by runtime character char_idx.
logic_summary: Single basic block. Issues the Watcom __CHK(0xC) stack/range probe emitted in the prologue, then calls fd2_pan_cursor_to_tile_animated(runtime_char[char_idx].pos_x, runtime_char[char_idx].pos_y) -- looking up the character's tile X/Y (uint8 fields at +0x00/+0x01 of the runtime_char struct via data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr) and delegating the animated step-by-step pan. No return value.

params.name: char_idx
params.semantics: Index into the runtime character array (data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr). Callers (AI turn focus, chapter init camera focus, attack/spell/item target preview, status query) pass the active actor/target slot index; the body uses it solely to index runtime_char[char_idx] for its pos_x/pos_y.
params.reason: Name is descriptive and accurate (an array index, not a position); no param_1 placeholder and no address residue.

returns.semantics: No return value; side effect is the animated camera/cursor pan performed by the callee.

notes: Source comment block (cursor.c lines 199-203) is already concise and correct ('Convenience: pan to runtime_char[char_idx]'s tile position.') -- kept verbatim, no Edit made. Ghidra plate is more detailed (shows __CHK(0xC) body + use cases) but does not contradict the src; left untouched. The decompiler's auto-named bPos_x/bPos_y byte fields correspond to the struct's pos_x/pos_y (types.h: runtime_char +0x00/+0x01 uint8), which the src already uses correctly. __CHK(0xC) is the Watcom stack-overflow/probe check inserted in the prologue, not game logic.
